definitions.explanation: An immediate understanding or knowing something without conscious reasoning; a hunch or sixth sense.

examples.japanese: {直感|ちょっかん}を{信|しん}じる。
{直感|ちょっかん}{的|てき}に{危険|きけん}だと{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I intuitively sensed it was dangerous.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{直感|ちょっかん}は{鋭|するど}く、いつも{正|ただ}しい。
examples.english: Her intuition is sharp and always correct.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{直感|ちょっかん}を{信|しん}じる - to trust one's intuition
・{直感|ちょっかん}が{働|はたら}く - intuition works/kicks in
・{直感|ちょっかん}が{鋭|するど}い - to have sharp intuition
・{直感|ちょっかん}{的|てき}（な） - intuitive

CONTRAST:
・{直感|ちょっかん} - immediate understanding without reasoning (cognitive)
・{本能|ほんのう} - innate, biological drives (instinct)
・{勘|かん} - a more casual word for intuition/hunch

USAGE:
The suru verb form {直感|ちょっかん}する means "to sense intuitively."
